identity.title: Grand Gulf Nuclear Station, Unit 1 Licensee Event Report 2023-001-01, Valve Closure Test Failure Resulting in Condition Prohibited by Technical Specification

cause.proximate_text: 1 E61 F003B valve disc traveling past the valve seat was caused by the splined adapter not being properly installed in the past per work order on October 27, 2017.
cause.theme: improper valve stem/spline reinstallation leading to mis-set travel stops

nodes.display_name: Disengagement between valve stem and drive sleeve
nodes.description: Slipped spline adapter caused the stem to disengage from the drive sleeve, so actuator moved and indicated open/closed without moving the valve stem.

nodes.display_name: Valve stem failed to move during 2017 surveillance
nodes.description: Operator observed no stem movement during Division 2 post-LOCA drywell vacuum breaker operability surveillance on 2017-10-26.

nodes.display_name: Valve disc traveling past the valve seat
nodes.description: 2023 diagnostic testing (with strain gauge) revealed the butterfly valve disc contacts the seat at 40 sec of a 60 sec stroke and continues traveling 20 sec past the seat, with actuator open/closed positions mis-set relative to true disc travel (60 deg open / 30 deg closed vs. correct 90-degree full travel).

chain: improper spline adapter installation (2017 WO) [cause X] -> spline adapter slips down stem -> stem disengages from drive sleeve -> (2017) no stem movement observed -> Division 2 purge/vacuum relief declared inoperable; and separately -> (2023) valve disc travels past seat (mis-set limit switches) -> condition prohibited by Tech Specs discovered retroactive to 2017-10-26
notes: This LER describes a long-latent condition: a 2017 spline-adapter installation defect caused an immediate surveillance failure (corrected at the time by reinstalling the adapter) but the underlying actuator/valve travel misalignment was not fully corrected until 2023, when strain-gauge diagnostic testing (implemented following a 2019 GL 96-05/JOG gap finding) revealed the disc traveling past the seat. The valve was retroactively declared to have been inoperable since 2017-10-26, making this a condition prohibited by Tech Specs. Cause code X ('Other') is used verbatim per form data despite the narrative describing what is essentially a maintenance/installation deficiency; category left as provided. No EIIS bracket codes given for valve/components in narrative; 'E61' system prefix taken from component IDs (1E61F003B) as the likely EIIS-style system designator for Drywell Purge, but since no explicit bracket or system name pairing was given, eiis_code is populated cautiously from the component ID prefix. Check valve 1E61F002B is mentioned only in a design/safety-significance context (backup flow prevention), not as an operable backup during the inoperability window, so no BACKED_UP_BY edge asserted for it -- included only as a Component for completeness per its explicit role description, though it could arguably be omitted as design context; retained since it has a specific identifier tied to the failure scenario mitigation path.
